title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', a continuation of La Longue Marche. He studies automorphisms φ^ of profinite Teichmüller-type groups, close to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^. The automorphisms act on π_{0,3}^, the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus three points (free profinite on two generators), and on an extension \hat{\mathfrak S}_{0,3}^+. That extension is π_{0,3}^ extended by finite symmetries ρ (order 3), σ_∞ and τ_∞, so that its quotient mod π_{0,3}^ is the symmetric group S_3.

Notation. Each φ^ is described by 'delicate parameters' and 'coarse parameters'.
- The delicate parameters are α ∈ π_{0,3}^·{1,τ_∞} and β ∈ π_{0,3}^. These are analogues of the f-component of a Drinfeld/Ihara pair (λ,f).
- The coarse parameters are cocycle-type expressions: ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1} and η = β σ(β)^{-1}. They are related by ξ = η l_1^ν, where l_1 is a loop and ν is presumably tied to the multiplier.
- α~ = α τ_∞^{α_3} is the normalised version of α lying in π_{0,3}^.

Formulas from the previous page.
- (47) φ^(ρ^{-1}(ξ)) = ρ^{j'} σ_∞^{α_3} ξ α~^{-1}, and its solved form (48) α~ = φ^(ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1})) ρ^{j'} σ_∞^{α_3}.
- (10)=(49) φ^(ξ) = β σ_∞^i, and its solved form (50) for β.

What this page does.
- It notes that the equivalence of (47) with (10)/(49), under the link ξ = η l_1^ν, deserves a direct verification. This is left undone.
- It stresses why these formulas matter: they express the delicate parameters α, β explicitly as values of φ^ on the coarse parameters ξ and ρ^{-1}(ξ).
- Both are identities in \hat{\mathfrak S}_{0,3}^+. Reducing mod π_{0,3}^ kills α~ and β, which lie in π_{0,3}^. This gives (51): the images in S_3 satisfy φ^·(ρ^{-1}(ξ)) = ρ^{j'} σ_∞^{α_3} and φ^·(ξ) = σ_∞^i.
- So the discrete invariants i, α_3 ∈ Z/12 and j' ∈ Z/3 are read off from the images of φ^(ξ) and φ^(ρ^{-1}(ξ)) in S_3.

The open question he poses. Can i and j', like α_3, be expressed through the multiplier μ (the cyclotomic-character-like scalar of φ^), or even through arbitrary residues ε_ℓ(μ)? The margin asks whether (i, α_3, j') can be read as a value in Z/12 × Z/12 × Z/3.

The modulus 12 is suggestive of the abelianisation of SL_2(Z) (Z/12), i.e. of the genus-1 / modular-group side of the tower.

On the next page he multiplies (47) and (50), using the relation on ξ, ρ(ξ), ρ^2(ξ). This gives (52)–(53), which express β^{-1}α as well. The upshot: the three principal delicate parameters β, α and β^{-1}α are given by φ^ evaluated at ξ, ρ^{-1}(ξ) and ρ(ξ).
errors: Whether the reductions are internally consistent cannot be checked from the page alone. As written, (51) assigns exponents i, α_3 ∈ Z/12 to σ_∞, yet in S_3 the element σ_∞ has order 2. So either \hat{\mathfrak S}_{0,3}^+ mod π is larger than S_3 (e.g. a central or SL_2-type extension), or only residues of i, α_3 are actually determined. Grothendieck writes '𝔖_3', so the claim that the Z/12 values are 'exactly' given needs the right quotient.
Grothendieck himself flags that the equivalence (47) ⇔ (10) under ξ = η l_1^ν has not been verified directly. It is a gap, not an error.

ideas.what: Expressing the 'delicate' GT-type parameters (α, β) of an automorphism through the values of the automorphism on 'coarse' cocycle parameters ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Parametrisation of GT^ / automorphisms of profinite braid and mapping-class groups via f-components and cocycle conditions
ideas.where_published: The general programme is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this computation is unpublished.

ideas.what: Reduction mod π_{0,3}^ of identities in the extended group to obtain discrete invariants (i, α_3 ∈ Z/12, j' ∈ Z/3) of an automorphism
ideas.modern_name: Discrete invariants / characters of GT-like groups via finite quotients (S_3, abelianisation Z/12 of SL_2(Z))

ideas.what: Question whether these discrete invariants are determined by the multiplier μ (cyclotomic character) or its residues
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of GT^ discrete data with the cyclotomic character χ mod 12 / mod 3

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether the discrete invariants i and j' (and the triple (i, α_3, j') in Z/12 × Z/12 × Z/3) of his automorphisms are functions of the multiplier μ (cyclotomic character), as α_3 is, possibly via residues ε_ℓ(μ). He also leaves unverified the direct equivalence of his two presentations (47) and (10).
missed.quote: Il faudrait voir si i, j' peuvent, comme α_3, s'expliciter en termes des multiplicateurs μ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would give an explicit description of the finite-level (mod 12, mod 3) shadow of the GT^ action in terms of χ. It is a small but concrete check in the theory of GT and its genus-1 / SL_2(Z) variants. The answer is probably known implicitly (e.g. via the action on \hat{SL_2(Z)}^ab = Z/12), but I am unsure it is stated in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical working step in Grothendieck's unpublished GT-type computations: it solves for delicate parameters and reduces to finite invariants. It aligns with what Drinfeld, Ihara and Lochak–Schneps later formalised. The open question about expressing the Z/12, Z/3 invariants through the multiplier is a minor unfinished thread, not a striking result.
transcription_corrections: 'η = βσ_3(η)^{-1}' should almost certainly read 'η = βσ(β)^{-1}' (the image shows β σ_3(…)^{-1}). The cocycle is in β, not η.
Line 3: 'α ∈ π_{0,3}^{~∧}' — the image shows π_{0,3}^ with a tilde/hat decoration; most likely α ∈ π_{0,3}^·{1,τ_∞} or \tilde π_{0,3}^, consistent with the previous page.
Last line: 'voire en termes de ces' should be 'voire en termes des', continuing on the next page with 'restes quelconques ε_ℓ(μ)'.
Margin, tentative reading: 'et voir aussi si j' (ou (i,α_3,j')) peuvent [s'interpréter par] des valeurs dans Z/12 × Z/12 × Z/3'.
